A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TR/TALR quantization-aware training work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplements support reliable comparison despite retitling and reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original classification and object-detection experiments in Tables 1–4, together with original training analyses and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and analyses and additionally reports detailed training-time measurements in Table S7.

M1.justification: The transition counting, moving-average TR, TALR update, and latent-weight update remain unchanged in Eqs. (5), (10)–(12) and Algorithm 1. V3 Section 4.3 relocates the quantization schemes already described in v2 Appendix D.1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate classification on CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet and detection on MS COCO. The added timing breakdown uses already evaluated ImageNet models and introduces no distinct task or data coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same optimizers and QAT baselines. In particular, v2 Table A and v3 Table S1 retain PACT, QIL, QNet, DSQ, LSQ, LSQ+, EWGS, and Nagel et al.; the timing table uses existing optimizer comparators.

E3.justification: The retained evaluation procedures, bit-widths, training budgets, schedules, and hyperparameters match, including v2 Table G and v3 Table S8. The expanded timing report supplies hardware and numerical details without establishing a changed training or testing procedure.

E4.justification: V3 adds an optimizer/model-specific computational-overhead analysis in Section S2.5 and Table S7, extending v2's brief 2% overhead statement. Existing scheduler, initial/final TR, optimizer, and TALR-update analyses and detection case studies are retained.

E5.justification: V2 Table F and v3 Table S6 report the same means and standard deviations over five random runs for the final-TR experiment. No additional repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests are introduced.

E6.justification: V3 Table S7 newly reports plain/TR-scheduled training times of 174/176 GPU-hours for SGD, 175/178 for Adam, and 477/492 for AdamW. Existing accuracy, AP, ablation values, training curves, and qualitative detection findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 changes the definition of δt from adjacent-level spacing to a post-scaling factor while retaining Eqs. (7)–(9). For binary values {-1, 1}, spacing is twice the multiplying scale, so the retained factor 1/2 in Eq. (8) no longer aligns clearly with the revised definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about scheduling transitions, controlling quantized-weight changes through TALR, and improving training across models and optimizers. The title change does not redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: V3 removes Section 5.2's qualification that prior QAT studies use differing training/evaluation protocols and often lack released source code. This removes an explicit caveat concerning cross-paper comparisons; the central interpretations of convergence and latent-weight distributions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Table S7 newly identifies four A5000 GPUs and gives absolute training times for ResNet-18 and DeiT-T, whereas v2 only states relative overhead. Existing implementation choices and hyperparameters are retained, and both versions still describe code release as prospective.

R1.justification: The same 50 cited works remain, with unchanged substantive positioning relative to QAT, oscillation suppression, pseudo-quantization, and binary optimizers. Reference reordering, formatting, and removal of the duplicated bibliography are presentation changes.

P1.justification: V3 retitles the paper, condenses parts of related work, moves Appendix D.1 into main-text Section 4.3, simplifies subsection headings, and renumbers the supplement. The duplicated supplementary bibliography is removed, while most prose and the overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table S7, compresses main Tables 1, 2, and 4 into single-column displays, moves Figure 2 earlier, and rearranges the supplementary quantizer figures. Existing plots and detection examples retain their substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful hardware-specific timing evidence and makes the existing quantization scheme easier to find in Section 4.3. However, it removes the cross-paper protocol caveat and replaces the clear level-spacing definition of δt with wording that leaves binary Eq. (8)'s normalization ambiguous. These documentation gains and losses in qualification and mathematical clarity do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
